title: Home Office & Augusta Rule
description: Home-office deduction (regular versus Rev. Proc. 2013-13 simplified method) and the IRC 280A(g) Augusta-rule day test from a square-footage and expense profile. The gross-income cap applies to both methods; the simplified method is not selectable for an S-corp owner-employee. The 280A(g)(1) bar on the corporate rent deduction is an open legal question: the figure is kept and flagged, not decided.

office_sq_ft.description: Square feet of the home used for business. Blank or 0 falls back to 0.

home_sq_ft.description: Total home square feet. Blank or 0 falls back to 1 to avoid dividing by zero.

business_use_pct.description: Business-use percent, 0 to 100. Null auto-derives office_sq_ft / home_sq_ft; 0 overrides to 0%.

annual_rent_usd.description: Annual rent or mortgage interest and taxes for the home, USD.

utilities_usd.description: Annual utilities for the home, USD.

other_home_expenses_usd.description: Other annual home expenses (insurance, repairs), USD. One undifferentiated bucket.

gross_business_income_usd.description: Gross business income used for the gross-income cap, USD. Free-standing figure.

entity_type_ho.description: Home-office filer: soleProp (Schedule C) or scorp (S-corp owner-employee, accountable plan).

rental_days.description: Days the home is rented to the business. The day test passes at 14 or fewer.

daily_rental_rate_usd.description: Fair-market daily rental rate charged to the business, USD.

corp_tax_rate_pct.description: Rate valuing the corporate rent deduction, percent. 0 falls back to 37.

entity_type_aug.description: Entity paying the rent: soleProp or scorp.

owner_marginal_rate_pct.description: Owner marginal rate, percent. 0 falls back to 32.

output_schema.description: output_payload: refusal_reason (null unless refused), echoes office_sq_ft, home_sq_ft, business_use_fraction, gross_business_income_usd, entity_type_ho, rental_days, daily_rental_rate_usd, corp_tax_rate, owner_marginal_rate, entity_type_aug; home office total_home_expenses_usd, regular_deduction_before_gross_income_cap_usd, regular_deduction_usd, simplified_deduction_before_gross_income_cap_usd, simplified_deduction_usd, simplified_method_selectable, simplified_wins_on_amounts, best_home_office_deduction_usd, best_home_office_method ('Regular'|'Simplified'), gross_income_cap_applied_to ('regular'|'both'); Augusta rule total_rental_income_usd, qualifies_280a_g_day_test, augusta_tax_free_income_usd, augusta_corp_deduction_usd, augusta_tax_benefit_usd, augusta_tax_benefit_at_owner_rate_usd; benefits home_office_tax_benefit_usd, combined_tax_benefit_usd, combined_tax_benefit_at_owner_rate_basis_usd; provenance switches{}, fallback_fields[] (objects with field, apex_fallback, raw_input), compliance_flags[], notes[]. On a refusal (non-finite input, a wrong-typed numeric, an unlisted entity_type_ho or entity_type_aug, or a non-object input), output_payload carries a refusal_reason code, every computed field null, and compliance_flags ['ART753_INPUT_REFUSED'].

refusal_reason.description: Null on a computed result; otherwise a refusal code (REFUSED_NON_FINITE_INPUT, REFUSED_INPUT_NOT_OBJECT, REFUSED_WRONG_TYPE_<FIELD>, REFUSED_ENTITY_TYPE_HO_NOT_ALLOWED, REFUSED_ENTITY_TYPE_AUG_NOT_ALLOWED).

input_schema_provenance: One property per input the kernel reads, 13 in total, each with a real type taken from that read: nine 'number', one ['number','null'] for business_use_pct because the kernel branches on its presence, and two 'string' + enum for the entity selectors. All 13 are required because compute() dereferences every one of them unconditionally; Apex's own per-field fallbacks apply only to a null or omitted value and are reported in fallback_fields, so a default is never mistaken for an input. The kernel refuses a wrong-typed numeric and any entity value outside the two enums, each with its own refusal code; it never coerces a caller value.
author: PostOakLabs

notes: §280A(g) has two conditions: the dwelling unit must be "used during the taxable year by the taxpayer as a residence" AND "actually rented for less than 15 days during the taxable year" (26 U.S.C. §280A(g), fetched 2026-10-06). This node tests only the day count — no input records residence status — so qualifies_280a_g_day_test is a day-count test, not a §280A(g) determination.

rental_days is the count you plan to rent (Apex #139 control label: "Days You Plan to Rent to Business"); §280A(g) tests days "actually rented". A plan is not an actual rental; the statutory test is retrospective and this node reads no calendar.

gross_business_income_usd is a free-standing whole-business figure. Rev. Proc. 2013-13 §2.06 states the §280A(c)(5) limitation as "the gross income derived from that use for the taxable year reduced by (1) the deductions allocable to the use that are allowable for the taxable year whether or not the unit is used as described in §280A(c)(1) through (4) … and (2) the allowable trade or business expenses that are not allocable to the use of the dwelling unit"; §4.08(2) restates it for the safe harbor. No Form 8829 mechanic is modelled, so the cap's scope is unverified.

entity_type_aug=scorp with rental_days<=14: the owner excludes the rental income under §280A(g)(2) and the corporation books the rent deduction. CAUTION: §280A(g)(1) says "no deduction otherwise allowable under this chapter because of the rental use of such dwelling unit shall be allowed" — on its face that bars this very deduction; practitioners split on whether the S-corp deduction survives. The figure is retained from Apex #139 and flagged, not endorsed (DIFFERS-06; OPEN QUESTION 1 in APEXPORT-139-REPORT.md).

other_home_expenses_usd is a single bucket whose Apex #139 hint lists "Insurance, repairs, depreciation (optional)"; a taxpayer using the safe harbor method "cannot deduct any depreciation (including any additional first-year depreciation) or §179 expense for the portion of the home that is used in a qualified business use" (Rev. Proc. 2013-13 §4.06), so a depreciation-bearing bucket distorts the regular-vs-simplified comparison.
